research.statement: For Z=q(S), the categorical score is E[S|Z] and I_q=Var(E[S|Z])=Σ_b W_b μ_b μ_b^T=Σ_b m_b m_b^T/W_b.
research.title: Quantized Fisher-information identity

research.statement: I_full-I_q=E[Cov(S|Z)] is positive semidefinite; hard quantization cannot increase Fisher information.
research.title: Exact Fisher-information loss decomposition

research.statement: rank(I_q)<=min(d,K-1); positive-definite full-D information requires K>=d+1.
research.title: Rank ceiling for K hard categories

research.statement: R=I_full^{-1/2} I_q I_full^{-1/2} satisfies 0<=R<=I, so every retention eigenvalue lies in [0,1].
research.title: Normalized retained-information spectrum

research.statement: eta_D=(det I_q/det I_full)^(1/d), the geometric mean retained Fisher information over normalized parameter directions.
research.title: D-efficiency relative to unbinned inference

research.statement: Report normalized retention eigenvalues, geometric mean, arithmetic mean, and minimum; D optimization alone does not guarantee equal retention in every direction.
research.title: Direction-resolved retained-information diagnostics

research.statement: eta_Ds=(det Schur_ψ(I_q)/det Schur_ψ(I_full))^(1/s).
research.title: Ds-efficiency relative to unbinned profiled inference

research.statement: Under an invertible local parameter transformation, I_q transforms by congruence and logdet changes only by a quantizer-independent constant.
research.title: D-optimal partition invariance under invertible reparameterization

research.statement: d-tr(I_full^{-1}I_q)=E||z-E[z|Z]||^2 for z=I_full^{-1/2}s; maximizing retained normalized trace is weighted k-means.
research.title: Normalized trace equals Fisher-whitened k-means

research.statement: For every centroid μ_c, μ_c^T I^{-1}μ_c<=1/W_c, and for δ=μ_a-μ_b, δ^T I^{-1}δ<=1/W_a+1/W_b.
research.title: D leverage inequality

research.statement: For a weighted point moved from non-singleton a to b, ΔI=αu_a u_a^T-βu_b u_b^T with α=wW_a/(W_a-w), β=wW_b/(W_b+w).
research.title: Exact weighted rank-two relocation

research.statement: With H=I^{-1}, q_aa=u_a^T H u_a, q_bb=u_b^T H u_b, q_ab=u_a^T H u_b, the determinant ratio is (1+αq_aa)(1-βq_bb)+αβq_ab^2; equivalently ΔF_D=log of that ratio wherever both determinants are positive.
research.title: Exact finite D log-determinant gain

research.statement: Accepting only exact positive D gains strictly increases the objective, cannot cycle, and terminates finitely at a one-point exchange-stable state.
research.title: Monotone exact D one-point exchange

research.statement: For distinct positive-weight score atoms obtained by merging duplicate rows, positive-definite retained information, exactly K nonempty cells, no move constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells, and zero-tolerance exact stability, every tied-or-worse nearest-centroid comparison from a non-singleton source has strictly positive exact D gain. Stability forces distinct centroids; singleton rows are then strictly nearest to their own centroids. Hence one-point exchange stability implies strict self-consistent D-Voronoi geometry.
research.title: Finite D exchange stability implies strict self-consistent Voronoi

research.statement: Every exact zero-tolerance one-point-exchange-stable positive-definite finite D solution on merged distinct positive-weight score atoms compiles to q_hat(s)=argmin_b (s-μ_b)^T I_hat^{-1}(s-μ_b), reproducing all merged-atom training labels strictly; original duplicate rows inherit the merged label. Positive solver tolerance gives only a tolerance-stamped boundary-disagreement guarantee.
research.title: Exact finite inductive closure / compiler

research.statement: Every finite global D optimum is exchange stable and therefore strict self-consistent D-Voronoi; unrestricted finite D optimization and realizable affine/Voronoi labeling optimization have the same optimum value.
research.title: Every finite global D optimum is geometrically realizable

research.statement: Because global optima are affine/Voronoi-realizable, arrangement enumeration yields an exact algorithm N^{O(Kd)} for fixed d and K.
research.title: Exact finite D optimization is XP for fixed (d,K)

research.statement: For unassigned U, I_completion <= I_partial+Σ_{i∈U} w_i s_i s_i^T, so its logdet is a valid upper bound on every completion.
research.title: Singleton-refinement branch-and-bound upper bound for D

research.statement: A batch Lloyd/Voronoi reassignment may be used as a proposal, but monotonicity is restored only by accepting proposals that improve the exact D objective.
research.title: Guarded D-Lloyd proposal is monotone when accepted by exact objective

research.statement: Self-consistent nearest-centroid assignment under the current D metric is strictly weaker than one-point exact exchange stability.
research.title: D-Voronoi fixed point does not imply exchange stability

research.statement: If coincident positive-weight score atoms may occupy different singleton cells, a positive-definite labeling can be vacuously one-point exchange stable while strict nearest-centroid assignment and deterministic score-only label reproduction fail.
research.title: Split duplicate atoms defeat strict D-Voronoi closure

research.statement: Batch recomputation of I^{-1}, nearest-centroid reassignment, and centroid update can decrease the true logdet objective.
research.title: Adaptive Mahalanobis Lloyd need not increase D

research.statement: For POI ψ and nuisance λ, S_ψ(I)=I_ψψ-I_ψλ I_λλ^{-1} I_λψ and F_s=logdet S_ψ(I)=logdet I-logdet I_λλ when the relevant blocks are nonsingular.
research.title: Ds objective is the logdet of efficient/profiled Schur information

research.statement: For full-data efficient score S_hat=S_ψ-B* S_λ, every quantizer satisfies Schur_ψ(I_q) <= Var(E[S_hat|q(S)]) in Loewner order.
research.title: Full-data efficient-score domination

research.statement: For d_ψ=1, deterministic D-optimal quantization of a scalar efficient score has ordered interval cells, and the finite-sample optimum can be solved exactly by dynamic programming.
research.title: Scalar efficient-score upper problem is exactly solvable by dynamic programming

research.statement: At a one-point exchange-stable Ds state, every admissible move satisfies s_aa - s_bb <= beta q_aa q_bb <= w_i q_aa q_bb (efficient-semimetric violation bounded by the product of full-metric leverages); no balancedness or mass margin needed, complementing DS-OKN-BOUND.
research.title: Exact profiled leverage stability bound

research.statement: Positive first-order efficient-semimetric margin need not imply positive exact finite Ds gain; exchange stability does not force exact finite efficient-Voronoi assignment.
research.title: D-style finite exchange-to-geometry theorem fails for Ds

research.statement: An exact centered equal-weight N=8,d=2,d_ψ=1,K=3 exhaustive example has a unique global Ds optimum that violates its own efficient-semimetric nearest-cell rule.
research.title: A finite global Ds optimum can be non-geometric

research.statement: For i.i.d. samples from an atomless law with finite second moments and a uniform affine-slab margin, one-point exchange-stable finite Ds labelings satisfying mass, conditioning, and projected-centroid-separation margins are asymptotically geometric (vanishing disagreement with their own efficient-semimetric companion rule); subsequential limits are self-consistent, hence population-stationary, efficient-Voronoi quantizers with convergent values; global finite optima converge in value to the population optimum over the margin-compatible geometric class, attained by their limits. Without the separation margin the same conclusions hold for the reduced (merged) rule.
research.title: Conditional finite-to-population Ds bridge

research.statement: For d_psi = d_lambda = 1 and score laws with conditionally centered nuisance (E[S_lam|shat]=0: Gaussian, elliptical), atomless efficient-score marginal with a unique optimal scalar K-quantizer (log-concave suffices) and swap-rich nuisance conditionals, almost surely along exact global finite Ds optima: (i) the value converges to the unrestricted population supremum v_K over all measurable K-cell quantizers, attained only by the optimal efficient-score interval quantizer, which is fully nuisance-degenerate and infeasible in-bin (zero nuisance block; DS9 feasibility split); (ii) cell masses converge to the positive population masses - the mass margin (M2) is automatic and singleton cells die out (the N<=18 singleton evidence is pre-asymptotic); (iii) the binned nuisance and cross blocks vanish, so lambda_min(I_N) -> 0: the conditioning margin (M3) FAILS for every kappa>0 and every law in the class - the optimizer sheds binned nuisance information by design; (iv) the margin-compatible optimum v*(kappa) is strictly below v_K, so DS14 governs margin-certified (necessarily suboptimal by delta(kappa)>0) solutions, never free global optima, on this class; (v) DS11(a) efficient-score domination becomes an equality at optima. The (M5) projected-centroid object rides on a 0/0 slope and degenerates with the metric; the meaningful reduced geometry is the scalar J* geometry with distinct centroids. The originally registered d_lambda-generality is refuted: at K = d_lambda + 1 exact centering forces every feasible labeling's profiled value to exactly zero (rank ceiling), so K >= d_lambda + 2 is the correct cardinality condition - at d_lambda = 1 that is exactly K >= 3.
research.title: Margins dichotomy at global finite Ds optima (conditionally centered laws, scalar nuisance)

research.statement: For d_psi = d_lambda = 1, conditionally centered laws (L) with scalar regularity (S), equal weights, centered empirical score rows, K >= 3: on one probability-one measurable event, simultaneously over every labeling at every N, (1) PRICE - for every kappa > 0 there is delta(kappa) > 0 with limsup_N sup{Phi_s_hat(z) : z feasible, I_hat_lambdalambda(z) >= kappa} <= v_K - delta(kappa), where sup(empty) = -infinity; since lambda_min(I_hat) <= I_hat_lambdalambda, the DS14 conditioning margin (M3) forces the same cap, and stability, optimality, selection measurability, and seeding are irrelevant; (2) FUNNEL - any feasible sequence with Phi_s_hat -> v_K has cells converging in sample measure to J*, min cell mass -> min_b w*_b > 0, and I_hat_lambdalambda, I_hat_psilambda, lambda_min -> 0, so DS15's degeneracy is value-topological; (3) FLOOR - label raw i.i.d. scores by any fixed measurable q with positive cell masses and I_q_lambdalambda > kappa, then compute information after exact sample centering: Phi_s_hat -> Phi(q), so the constrained empirical sup is asymptotically at least v*+(kappa) = sup{Phi(q) : I_q_lambdalambda > kappa} and v*+(kappa) <= v_K - delta(kappa). This neither asserts attainment nor continuity in kappa, and v*(kappa), defined instead by lambda_min(I_q) >= kappa, is only bounded above by v*+(kappa). (R) is not needed. Proof: Proposition 4 plus arbitrary-grouping rigidity using a compact tilt-codebook uniform law, and signed weighted-VC Glivenko-Cantelli over all tilted half-planes.
research.title: Margin price and value funnel at arbitrary finite Ds labelings

research.statement: For d_psi = d_lambda = 1 and any atomless law in class (L) (E[S_lambda | shat] = 0 a.s.) with E S = 0, E||S||^2 < oo, and I > 0: (POPULATION) every root-consistent strip rule, meaning E[h(T_beta) S_lambda] = 0, has binned nuisance block exactly zero at every tilt and K >= 2; equivalently, no regular tilt-consistent strip rule B*(I_q) = beta exists because that definition requires I_lambdalambda(q) > 0. Hence no full-rank bounded-packet stationary rule has pairwise-distinct projected centroids. (EMPIRICAL) if (M4) also holds, the pathwise audited DS14 bridge gives one selection-independent probability-one event on which, for fixed K and every rational kappa, c_0, gamma > 0, all sufficiently large N have no ordinary one-point exchange-stable K-cell labeling satisfying (M2)+(M3)+(M5). Neither (S) nor (R) is used. Thus OP30(a) full-triple inhabitation is disproved on this conditionally centered class; the conclusion does not extend to non-centered laws.
research.title: Conditional centering empties the margin-certified stable branch

research.statement: The registered theory gives five observable cases. (1) A concrete regular tilt-DP saddle closes p_reg=g_reg=d and certifies a finite global in-bin labeling; a singular saddle certifies only the generalized DS11 problem. (2) A nonclosed reported bracket reports its named interval, does not authorize the word optimal, and does not certify a duality gap either (a deterministic DP tie policy can hide a closure: CE-DS-TILT-DUAL-TIE-MASK-001). (3) The projected full-efficient-score interval rule remains the currently established unconditional compiler for the distinct projected problem with nuisance information supplied externally. (4) A profiled DS14 companion rule is theorem-backed only along sequences satisfying every audited DS14 law, stability, mass, conditioning, compactness, and projected-separation hypothesis; one measured floor or finite root is diagnostic only. (5) Otherwise compilation of a profiled terminal is refused. On class (L), DS16/DS17 keep the full-triple ordinary-stable companion branch priced and eventually empty. Off (L), DS18 plus DS19 prove that the beta-zero interval DP is Delta-consistent on one exact law, but this value transfer is deliberately not a compile authorization. Strong tilt duality can fail by order one, and the multivariate outer problem is nonquasiconvex.
research.title: Profiled compile verdict is selected by an observable certificate state

research.statement: For d_psi=1 and positive finite weights, write V_z(beta)=btw(S_psi-beta S_lambda;z) (uncentered), v_K(beta)=max_z V_z(beta), and Phi^+(z)=min_beta V_z(beta). The DP-active generalized primal p^+, generalized global value g^+, regular in-bin primal p_reg, regular global value g_reg, and dual d=min_beta v_K(beta) obey p^+ <= g^+ <= d and p_reg <= g_reg <= g^+ <= d; d is attained after quotienting the common nuisance-null space. The generalized bracket closes, p^+=g^+=d, iff some labeling z in the DP-optimal set D(beta) at some beta satisfies beta I_lambdalambda(z)=I_psilambda(z); then every Phi^+-maximiser and every dual minimiser form such a pair; if the exhibited z has a nonsingular nuisance block it is an ordinary in-bin global optimum, otherwise it certifies only the DS11 pseudo-inverse problem. Fixed-tilt exact rational evaluation of v_K, an active labeling, the exact one-sided derivatives and the primal values costs O(KN^2) rational operations (O(KN) after sorting) and tolerates exact ties in every tie order (tie lemma). A certified rational epsilon-bracket on d is computable in time polynomial in the input bits and log(1/epsilon) via an observable coercivity radius, a subgradient separation oracle and a cutting-plane LP lower certificate. Exact minimisation is polynomial in bit complexity at d_lambda=1 for every K (root-separation bisection on the one-sided DP derivatives, output rational or a degree-2 algebraic number), and polynomial in arithmetic operations for fixed d_lambda>=2 and variable K (Toledo 1993 parametric search). Exact polynomial bit complexity for fixed d_lambda>=2 with variable K, and any exact statement for variable d_lambda, is OPEN-DS-TILT-DUAL-EXACT-COMPLEXITY.
research.title: Scalar-POI tilt-DP gives a valid two-sided certificate with an exact saddle closure gate

research.statement: An exact equal-weight N=4, K=3, d_psi=d_lambda=1 table (CE-DS-TILT-DUAL-GAP-001) has all six nonempty partitions regular, global profiled value 116805/11816, and tilt dual at least 61717893/5839400 by an exact convex mixture of two active partition quadratics; its exact dual minimum is 44729/4232 at the rational crossing beta*=-8/23, so the exact gap is 534361/781333 > 0.68 even though the DS9 and DS11 domains coincide. The witness is support-minimal for K=3. The overall support minimum is N=3, K=2: CE-DS-TILT-DUAL-GAP-002 (rows (-1,0),(0,-1),(1,0), equal weights) has g^+=1/3 and exact d=1/2 at beta*=0, gap 1/6, with a fully rational mixture proof. A positive-weight bounded augmentation family with vanishing added mass preserves the global-versus-dual gap asymptotically, so the gap is Theta(1), not a finite-grid artifact.
research.title: The scalar-POI tilt dual can have an order-one strong-duality gap

research.statement: An exhaustive finite example with a simple minimum eigenvalue has a global E optimum whose vv^T nearest-cell rule disagrees with a training label.

research.statement: For hard affine/Voronoi parameterizations, finite empirical labels and cell moments remain unchanged until a training row crosses a boundary; ordinary gradient is therefore zero almost everywhere.
research.title: Hard finite geometric objective is piecewise constant in boundary parameters

research.statement: For probabilities r_ib, W_b=Σ_i w_i r_ib and m_b=Σ_i w_i r_ib s_i give I_soft=Σ_b m_bm_b^T/W_b, the Fisher information of the corresponding randomized categorical observation when the randomization rule is theta-independent.

research.statement: A positive-temperature softmax affine-max family is smooth on the regular region; line-search gradient/quasi-Newton methods can be monotone in the soft objective and converge only to standard stationary notions.

research.statement: Because the objectives depend only on (W_b,m_b), atomless purification implies randomized and deterministic quantizers have the same attainable population objective values.
research.title: Randomized and deterministic population optima coincide for moment-based criteria under atomlessness

research.statement: For a compact finite-capacity affine-max class with uniform cell-mass and conditioning margins and appropriate score integrability, cell moments converge uniformly; objective values converge uniformly; approximate empirical maximizers are value-consistent, and isolated population optima give decision/parameter consistency up to labels.
research.title: Restricted affine-max empirical consistency

research.statement: Determine whether min_beta v_K(S_psi-beta S_lambda), with K and d_lambda part of the rational input, admits exact algebraic optimization in polynomial bit complexity using the fixed-tilt interval-DP oracle, including active tie refinements, without materializing a potentially large parametric-DP envelope. Settled by DS-TILT-DUAL-CERTIFICATE and its audit: fixed-tilt exact evaluation, polynomial certified-epsilon minimization, exact polynomial-bit minimization at d_lambda=1 for every K (root-separation bisection), and exact minimization in polynomially many arithmetic operations for fixed d_lambda>=2 with variable K (Toledo 1993 fixed-dimension parametric search with degree-2 comparisons). Remaining: a polynomial bit bound for fixed d_lambda>=2 with variable K (a root-separation argument for the conic breakpoint arrangement carried through the parametric search), and any exact statement, or hardness obstruction, for variable d_lambda.
research.title: Exact bit complexity of the variable-dimension tilt-DP dual

research.statement: Complete the academic margins dichotomy beyond the audited d_psi=d_lambda=1 DS15 class. For d_psi>1, establish the required uniqueness and rigidity theory for vector-D quantization of the efficient score before transferring the degenerate-attainer argument. For d_lambda>=2 and K>=d_psi+d_lambda+1, construct or refute a vector-(R) steering mechanism spanning all nuisance directions. The rank-vacuous boundary K=d_psi+d_lambda is already excluded by CE-DS-MARGINS-RANK-VACUITY-001. The deployment-facing non-centered DS18 remainder is closed by DS19's value-consistent interval-DP primal and is not part of this P6 question.
research.title: Vector-parameter margins dichotomy beyond the scalar DS15 class

research.statement: Resolve the two academic remainders left by DS17 on the scalar conditionally centered class: whether ordinary exchange-stable empirical sequences can track (M5)-free coincident-centroid wasted-cell configurations, and whether the constrained values v*(kappa) and v*+(kappa) are attained and one-sided continuous under their distinct DS16 conventions. The Gaussian sign-split construction proves only nonemptiness of the closed population feasible class for kappa<=1/pi. Deployment and non-centered Delta-selection are closed out of P1 by DS19 and are not part of this P7 question.

research.statement: Develop influence-function or bootstrap confidence intervals for reported retention functionals (e.g. geometric-mean retention), handling the non-smoothness of hard assignment at cell boundaries, so retention is reported with error bars rather than as a point estimate. Settled special case (5 Sep 2026, RETENTION-PLUGIN-CLT-FROZEN-SCALAR): frozen rule, scalar true score, iid equally weighted oracle-score evaluation sample - the plug-in ratio is asymptotically normal with a consistent influence-function variance and a valid Wald interval whenever sigma^2 > 0. Still open: vector scores and the geometric-mean retention (det R)^(1/d) as a matrix functional of the same moments; rules refitted on the evaluation sample, where the boundary non-smoothness enters; weighted samples; any uncertainty statement without an oracle score; and the degenerate second-order limit of n(eta_hat - eta) when sigma^2 = 0 (eta in {0, 1} or two-atom cells), where the Wald interval is measured to be conservative with width O(1/n). The special case was independently audited 5 Sep 2026 (AUDITS/AUDIT-SCORE-ORACLE-ROBUSTNESS-001.md): verified with the sigma^2 = 0 wording hardened at eta = 0. Literature-first pass for the vector case run 5 Sep 2026 (LITERATURE/audits/RETENTION-PLUGIN-CLT-FROZEN-VECTOR-5-September-2026.md): the vector CLT is the delta method plus the determinant differential with influence functions already in Radhakrishnan & Kshirsagar (1981) and fourth-moment canonical-correlation asymptotics in Muirhead & Waternaux (1980); the geometric-mean form on a fixed partition with uncentred moments, the plug-in variance and the endpoints are the search gap the packet RETENTION-PLUGIN-VECTOR now targets.
research.title: Finite-sample uncertainty for retention estimates
